notes:
Inbound SMB POC. Team: PM (Aisha), 2 backend engs (python stack), 1 frontend. Primary goal: replace brittle webhook-based action runner with model tool-calling + streaming structured output to drive UI actions in near-real-time.

Symptoms observed: streaming responses sometimes produce invalid JSON chunks when client attempts to parse mid-stream. Customer uses SSE -> front-end JSON.parse on buffer; when "function_call" arrives split across chunks parser fails. Also saw function schema mismatch: customer defined function schema with 'quantity' as integer but their app sends string; model sometimes emits strings which fail strict schema validators. Examples: "\"parameters\": {\"order_id\": \"123\", \"quantity\": \"2\"}" expected integer. They also hit "unexpected additional properties" due to model returning small metadata fields not in schema.

What we covered on calls: quick fixes and mitigations: (1) advise buffering until complete JSON object detected (closing brace + newline) before parsing client-side; (2) recommend explicit function schemas with types matching app types; (3) enable structured-json mode (JSON_MODE) + strict function calling to reduce free-form text; (4) use top-level streaming events for function_call only to avoid interleaved assistant text.

Customer quote: "When the UI tries to execute action, it crashes — we see 'Unexpected token' in console. Feels like partial frames are being parsed."

Current status: trial account on hosted_api. Low volume but latency sensitive (target 200-400ms p95 for chat actions). Cost sensitivity moderate. They want to keep on public cloud; SSO + audit logging are checkboxes for later.

Open engineering notes / leads: Evan to reproduce with customer's exact python SSE client (attached logs in Gmail thread). We suspect two root causes: streaming boundary semantics + schema/type drift in function params. Proposed repro steps: reproduce SSE stream using their request headers, confirm chunk boundary that causes parse error, then test server-side options: (a) set function_call behavior to 'strict' or 'none' to compare, (b) enable structured output mode, (c) run short test w/ quantized batch to see timing changes.
